transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-18
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Crimson Peak Head of Cloud), Ethan Zhou (CTO), Lena Ortiz (Partnerships)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated, possibly noisy):
- Intro to Crimson Peak's channel ambitions for edge GPU consolidation and resale.
- Discussed Redwood Dedicated vs Private deployments for on-prem partners.
- Agreed to run a short pilot benchmark; Redwood to provide test harness; customer to provide workloads.

Topics: partner onboarding, pilot scope, security, pricing, routing/caching, kernerl selection (sic)

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, um welcome, thanks for joining. this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the partnership side. jordan my SE will go deep on the technicals after intros.
[00:12] Maya Singh: Thanks Alex, hi all, i'm Maya, Head of Cloud at Crimson Peak. we focus on edge GPU leasing and resale into the telco and retail edge market.
[00:20] Ethan Zhou: And I'm Ethan, CTO. we run a combination of micro dc installs and partner co-located racks, it's kinda hybrid.
[00:28] Lena Ortiz: Lena here, partnerships — curious about go-to-market / white-labeling, and margins.
[00:35] Jordan Patel: Hi, Jordan from Redwood. i'll mainly cover the runtime nuances and the integration points for private deployments and dedicated pools.
[00:42] Alex Kim: Great, quick agenda: 1) learn about Crimson Peak use cases, 2) talk integration model (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 3) pilot/bench plan + next steps.
[00:55] Maya Singh: Perfect. quick context — we currently resell bare VM GPU access and a small managed inference layer that customers hate because latency spikes. We want a better inference stack to offer as a managed product, and are evaluating partners to layer on — think: Redwood as the inference runtime and orchestration that we white-label.
[01:18] Jordan Patel: Sounds good. couple of questions up front — what's your typical request size (seq length, tokens), batch patterns, and do you need real-time <=100ms p95 for any customers?
[01:31] Ethan Zhou: Most telco use cases are short prompts, heavy small-batch (5–20 qps per endpoint) but with bursty spikes during events. retail uses are slightly longer for re-rank / personalization, maybe 512 tokens. We have customers who care about 200ms p50 and 500ms p95, but cost sensitivity is high.
[01:55] Jordan Patel: Ok — that aligns with workloads where prefix KV caching and selective batching can save cost without blowing latency. Our runtime supports continuous batching and automatic prefix caching; we can route low-latency tenants to dedicated pools and less-sensitive to cheaper quantized variants.
[02:12] Maya Singh: When you say quantized variants — do you mean we can run smaller models for some customers for price points? what's the model catalog look like?
[02:19] Alex Kim: Right, Redwood maintains a catalog — curated open models, and we can host customer models. For edge partner usage you could either surface Redwood-hosted models or deploy a Private stack in your co-located racks and we manage the control plane.
[02:34] Lena Ortiz: if we whiten label it, how do we handle billing and SLAs? do we mark up or white label the API?
[02:41] Alex Kim: There's a couple options. simple reseller model — we bill Crimson Peak at wholesale and you bill the end customers. full white-label — we can support a partner integration where calls are proxied through your gateway; that requires an integration layer and we can discuss co-branding. SLA mapping and pass-through terms we'd cover in the partner commercial doc.
[02:59] Ethan Zhou: Security — we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs for all calls. also data residency per region, and we sometimes need an air-gapped option.
[03:12] Jordan Patel: All supported. Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) provides a customer-managed network and you can integrate with your KMS/HSM. We also produce detailed audit logs and we have SOC2 in our hosted offering. For air-gapped there's an on-prem bundle we can evaluate for enterprise customers.
[03:29] Maya Singh: Ok good. one technical concern — network egress between our racks and the Redwood control plane, latency and also handshake for KV caches. how much of the runtime is local vs central?
[03:41] Jordan Patel: The runtime is edge-first when deployed private: inferencing happens locally on the GPUs — control plane pushes model artifacts and rollout configs. KV cache and prefix caching live in the runtime so they are local to the serving host. Only telemetry and aggregated metrics go back to the control plane unless you opt into full remote logging.
[03:58] Ethan Zhou: That helps. what about model updates / rollouts? can we do canary or A/B?
[04:04] Jordan Patel: Yes, rollouts are supported — canary, percent-based, and automatic fallback to a variant. In constrained capacity events we can fallback from high-precision variant to a quantized variant automatically.
[04:15] Maya Singh: We're curious about benching — we want real numbers to show to potential telco customers. do you provide a benchmark harness?
[04:22] Alex Kim: Yes, Jordan will share a lightweight harness. typically we run latency and throughput profiles for your typical sequence lengths and models. we also recommend profiling cold-start KV behavior and warm caches.
[04:35] Jordan Patel: I'll share a runner script and a spreadsheet template — it includes step-by-step: 1) airflow or k8s job to spin traffic, 2) sequence length distribution, 3) tokenization corner cases. we'll want one production-ish workload from you to make it meaningful.
[04:52] Lena Ortiz: On commercials, what's typical margin for a reseller — i know that's not exact but ballpark.
[04:59] Alex Kim: We can give tiered wholesale. margins depend on committed capacity and whether you resell hosted or run private. Dedicated/Reserved pricing improves unit economics; white-label fees apply if we manage the control plane for you. We'll share a sheet.
[05:12] Ethan Zhou: One more — runtime OS/hardware compatibility. our racks run a mix of A100s and newer accelerators, sometimes older T4-class. Does Redwood support mixed fleets?
[05:23] Jordan Patel: Yes, multi-architecture is supported. our compilation/kernel selector picks kernels based on architecture and sequence length profile. for older GPUs performance is lower but the runtime chooses quantization and batching strategies to stay within SLAs.
[05:36] Maya Singh: Any known limitations around local caching for distributed inference across multiple edge nodes? we sometimes need cross-node KV sync for session continuity.
[05:46] Jordan Patel: Cross-node sync is possible but we usually recommend sticky routing per session to keep KV local — cross-node replication is feasible but increases latency/cost. we can discuss a hybrid: async replication for non-critical state.
[06:02] Alex Kim: Quick safety note — we can enforce content filters and policy hooks pre- and post-inference if your customers need moderation.
[06:09] Lena Ortiz: Are there existing channel partners who do similar white-labels we can talk to?
[06:15] Alex Kim: We can connect you with one or two references — i'll include that in the partner doc. i won't name names on the call.
[06:22] Maya Singh: Would be helpful. also curious about support model — 24/7? tiered?
[06:27] Alex Kim: We have tiered support: standard business hours, and enterprise 24/7 with faster SLAs. for partners we usually offer a partner success manager and optionally a shared on-call.
[06:37] Ethan Zhou: Regarding pilot scoping — i'm thinking a 4-week pilot, run on one of our co-located racks with 2 A100s, use one telco customer workload and one retail workload, measure p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens. is that feasible?
[06:53] Jordan Patel: Totally feasible. timeline: week 1 deploy + baseline, week 2 run warm cache tests, week 3 stress/scaling tests, week 4 evaluate and tune (quantization/batching).
[07:05] Maya Singh: On billing for pilot — do you charge?
[07:08] Alex Kim: For pilots we often give a discounted pilot rate or credits for early partners; depends on whether Redwood manages infra or you provide it. we'll put options in the partner commercial doc.
[07:18] Lena Ortiz: Any regulatory or compliance red flags for telco deployments in APAC? data residency?
[07:24] Jordan Patel: Region-level controls are supported. for APAC we recommend Private deployments to ensure all data and models stay in-country; our KMS integrations can be regionally isolated.
[07:36] Ethan Zhou: Latency targets — some telco customers want <=100ms p95 for short prompts; you said you can route to dedicated pools — what's typical latency on A100 dedicated for 64-token prompts?
[07:46] Jordan Patel: On well-tuned stacks we can get sub-100ms p95 for small prompts on modern GPUs with a dedicated pool and prefix caching, but it depends on model architecture and tokenization. we can validate during bench.
[07:58] Maya Singh: One small ask — can we host the control plane in our VPC for partner accounts? we want to minimize external network hops for auth and metrics.
[08:05] Alex Kim: Yes — Redwood Private supports hosting a private control plane. that is a larger integration but commonly done for partners who want control plane egress minimized. we'll detail the options.
[08:17] Ethan Zhou: Any friction integrating our billing system? we use a self-billing invoicing flow and need programmatic usage records every hour.
[08:26] Alex Kim: We expose detailed usage APIs and can push usage files to an S3 endpoint or integrate with your billing system via webhook. hourly granularity is possible.
[08:36] Maya Singh: Ok this is useful. are there any PII/PHI restrictions baked in? a few of our customers handle identity signals in prompts.
[08:45] Jordan Patel: We support configurable retention policies and token-level redaction in transit. for PHI you'd want strict KMS and an on-prem stack; we can also sign BAAs for qualifying customers.
[08:57] Lena Ortiz: Onboard timeline — how fast could we go from signed SOW to pilot starting?
[09:02] Alex Kim: If it's hosted and you provide no special constraints, days. For private/dedicated with racks and control plane in your VPC, typically 2–6 weeks depending on connectivity and cert exchanges.
[09:15] Maya Singh: Great. can you also provide a simple reference architecture diagram for the co-located model?
[09:20] Jordan Patel: Yes i'll attach a reference diag in the partner doc — showing control plane, local runtime, telemetry flows, and KV cache placement.
[09:29] Ethan Zhou: Regarding the runtime footprint — what's the memory and disk requirements for model artifacts and KV cache per node?
[09:36] Jordan Patel: Depends on model size. typical 7B-class model + kv cache needs ~30–60 GB GPU memory for serving; artifacts on disk 20–50GB. we provide sizing guidance in the integration doc.
[09:51] Maya Singh: Any special networking requirements for high-throughput telemetry? we prefer to avoid saturating our mgmt plane.
[09:58] Jordan Patel: Telemetry can be batched and sent on a separate mgmt interface; we can push aggregated metrics only to save bandwidth.
[10:06] Alex Kim: ok want to pivot to next steps to capture commitments.
[10:10] Lena Ortiz: yes please.
[10:11] Alex Kim: Action items recap: 1) Redwood sends partner integration doc + pricing and references (Alex) — due 2027-08-20. 2) Jordan shares benchmark harness and reference architecture (Jordan) — due 2027-08-24. 3) Crimson Peak to share workload and target customer list (Maya) — due 2027-08-25. 4) schedule SE-led deep dive week of 2027-08-30.
[10:38] Maya Singh: Sounds good, thanks. one last quick Q: are there any non-starters for you on hardware types we should be aware of?
[10:45] Jordan Patel: Not really — older GPUs work but performance differs; we recommend at least one modern accelerator for low-latency customers.
[10:53] Ethan Zhou: Perfect. we'll get the workload files over. thanks Alex and Jordan.
[10:58] Alex Kim: thanks everyone. i'll send the doc and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[11:05] Lena Ortiz: thanks — bye.
